title: AI Spend Is Surging: How to Control Rising Cloud Costs
summary: Learn how to manage rising AI cloud costs with visibility, forecasting, and optimization strategies to reduce waste.
body_markdown:
AI adoption is accelerating across nearly every industry. From customer support to product development, teams are building AI features into the systems that run their business. That progress comes with a price tag few teams planned for.


AI applications lean hard on compute, storage, networking, and model inference. Each of these adds up quickly, and many companies watch their AI spending climb faster than expected.[According to Omdia](https://omdia.tech.informa.com/pr/2026/mar/global-cloud-infrastructure-spending-rose-29percent-in-q4-2025-as-hyperscalers-scaled-ai-infrastructure-investment) , global cloud infrastructure spending reached US$110.9 billion in the fourth quarter of 2025, up 29% year over year, with full-year spending hitting US$399.6 billion. Omdia expects that figure to grow another 27% in 2026, pushing total annual spending beyond US$500 billion.


The challenge is clear: how do you scale AI initiatives without letting cloud costs spiral out of control? This article breaks down why AI spending rises so fast, where the hidden costs hide, and the practical steps you can take to bring them under control.


## **Why is AI spending rising faster than most teams expect?**


AI does not behave like traditional software. Costs shift constantly, and usage tends to grow in ways that catch finance teams off guard.


### **Why do AI workloads demand so much infrastructure**


Training and running AI models requires serious horsepower. GPU-intensive training pulls heavy compute. Inference at scale, the day-to-day work of answering user requests, runs continuously and adds up. On top of that, AI systems need large volumes of data storage and processing power to function.


A single AI application can require more resources than a traditional business system. As cloud providers note, models must process large datasets and respond in near real time, which pushes companies to rely on high-performance cloud infrastructure rather than on-premises systems.


### **Why does AI usage grow faster than forecasts**


Most AI cost overruns start small. A team runs an experiment, the experiment works, and suddenly it becomes a production feature serving thousands of users. More teams adopt AI tools across the organization, and API and infrastructure consumption climbs with each new use case.


This pattern explains why budgets miss the mark. The same AI task can cost ten times more from one run to the next, and AI agents can burn real money in minutes through model calls, retries, and workflow loops, often without anyone noticing until the bill arrives weeks later.


## **What are the hidden costs of AI infrastructure?**


Your compute bill is only part of the story. While GPUs get the most attention, several other factors contribute to the total cost of running AI workloads, including:


-


Compute resources for model training and inference


-


Storage for datasets, logs, and model artifacts


-


Networking and data movement between services


-


Data transfer charges that grow as workloads scale


-


Managed AI and cloud services that often carry premium pricing


Because these costs are spread across multiple services, AI spending can become difficult to predict and control.


### **AI Tool Sprawl Creates Visibility Challenges**


It is very common today for companies to use multiple different AI tools, model providers, and cloud services all at the same time. Each one produces its own billing data, which can obscure total AI spending. This creates a visibility problem.


Recent studies show that[only 26% of companies understand their AI costs](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/technology/tech-news/kpmg-survey-just-showed-why-more-than-50-companies-may-be-in-for-a-rude-shock-on-their-ai-spending/articleshow/131587536.cms) . Without a centralized view, the costs and time associated with identifying AI spending and determining AI spending's impact are significantly greater.


## **Why do companies struggle to understand AI costs and ROI?**


When many companies spend more resources on AI, it is more difficult for them to confirm that the investment made was worthwhile. Many companies can identify the spending that is incurred to pay for AI, but very few can connect the spending to any benefits that may be received.


One reason for this confusion is that spending may be incurred to pay for many different AI services. Companies may have to pay separate services that provide data, observability tools, and services that allow companies to provide their own models. Instead of a single payment, teams have to track spending from many vendors.


When teams have to track spending from many vendors, it makes forecasting spending more difficult. If spending is difficult to forecast, it’s difficult to determine who is responsible for the budget. Without tracking total spending, it’s difficult to identify areas for improvement and determine the value of AI services.


As AI services take up a larger part of the budget, visibility of spending is important for managing costs.


## **What are the most effective ways to reduce AI infrastructure costs?**


Here are three proven approaches to manage rising AI infrastructure costs:


**1. Improve resource utilization**


Be sure to only pay for resources used. This can include:


-


**Rightsizing:** Ensuring the correct provision of resources necessary to meet the workload demands


-


**Eliminating idle resources:** Turn off servers that are not in use.


-


**Scheduling workloads:** Expensive compute resources should be activated only when necessary.


**2. Use commitments and discounts**


The most consistently cost-effective way to run workloads in the cloud is via discounts for committed usage ([Savings Plans](https://www.pump.co/blog/aws-savings-plans/) ,[Reserved Instances](https://www.pump.co/blog/aws-reserved-instances/) , and[Committed Use Discounts](https://www.pump.co/blog/google-cloud-cuds/) ). The biggest risk to using discounts happens when committed resources are unused commitments. This often makes teams reluctant to make these commitments.


**3. Monitor and forecast AI spending**


Costs cannot be controlled without having a clear picture of where resources are being consumed. Effective cost allocation should make it possible to avoid problems while providing a framework for planning. While spending forecasts are important for most organizations, they are essential for those groups that are rapidly scaling AI services.

## **Conclusion**


AI spending will keep rising as more workloads move into core business systems. That trend is not slowing down.[Accel projects global AI and cloud spend will surpass US$1 trillion by 2030](https://kpmg.com/xx/en/our-insights/value-creation/future-forward.html) .

## **Frequently asked questions**


### **Why is AI infrastructure so expensive?**


AI infrastructure consumes a lot of resources because of the amount of computation and storage required to train a model, the need for large-scale, constant inference, and the large amount of networking as a result of model training. Major cloud providers bill for each of compute, storage, transfer, and time, making costs very high and hard to estimate.


### **How can companies reduce AI infrastructure costs?**


AI infrastructure costs can be controlled by better utilization of resources (right-sizing and removing idle resources), offerings that provide costs up-front, like Savings Plans and Reserved Instances, and more careful cost forecasting and tracking. Tools like[Pump do cost optimization automatically](https://www.pump.co/) and reduce cloud costs by 60%.


### **How do you measure AI ROI?**


Measuring AI ROI means connecting each AI dollar to the outcome it produces, by customer, product, team, or workflow. This is difficult with siloed billing data, which is why only 14% of CFOs can currently prove AI ROI.


### **What is AI spend management?** .


Managing AI spend has to do with maintaining control over and optimizing the amount of money that is consumed by AI workloads and tools. This encompasses a lot of visibility across the cloud and various model providers, as well as creating performance thresholds that have a clear cost and employing strategies that remove overspending.
